utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Yes, before we start this morning, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we had a problem yesterday on a question you put to the witness, whether it was on the road or down the road. And you indicated it might have been a translation problem as far as the testimony of the witness was concerned. It was a translation problem, but in a totally different respect. That is, that the question as you put it in French to the witness, where you said "sous la route," was in the English translation as "on the road." So therefore, it was the translation of your question that caused some confusion. But there was -- it was -- you're perfectly right that it was a translation matter rather than anything you would have not precise in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, indeed, Mr. President. But it is very hard for me to listen to the questions and to look at the people and to ask the questions and to watch the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We all have similar problems where we are trying to catch all the languages, if possible, for me only two of them. But the matter has been settled, and your question represented perfectly what the witness would have said according to the French and the English transcript. Mr. Usher, could you please -- Mr. Ierace, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Firstly, I have those colour photographs which I could hand up at this stage. It's of the Orthodox church. We have added an A to the end of the exhibit number to distinguish them. They are P3753A. I hand up those copies. Secondly, in relation to this witness, we again had a problem with the 65 ter summary. It refers to incident 22 but gives no inkling at all of what the witness would say about that incident. I have spoken to my learned colleague this morning about that, and we have been given some information which hopefully will cover it. But I simply wish to emphasise the difficulty the Prosecution is placed in in not having an appropriate summary of facts pursuant to the directions which you have given. It should have been provided to us in writing a long time ago. Secondly, we were told a few days ago that the witness would be shown some photographs which came into evidence through the Prosecution witness Henneberry. The 65 ter summary gives no suggestion at all as to how those photographs could be relevant. I've spoken to my learned colleague about that this morning, and I'm told that the witness may have met Mr. Henneberry or did meet Mr. Henneberry in May, had something to say about his character. And that's as far as it goes. So Mr. President, in summary, we still have significant problems in terms of 65 ter summaries coming from the Defence. Thank you. I should add to the photographs show gun positions at Lima 7, and Mr. Henneberry, in other photographs standing alongside military equipment. And we've had to refresh our memory on what evidence Mr. Henneberry gave without any assistance about what the witness might say about his evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Are you going to ask to put questions to the witness in respect of the testimony of Mr. Henneberry?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no. I just want to inform the Chamber that Saturday, we spoke to the witness. And in the summary and the information about the cooperation in the presence of UNPROFOR in the part of city where she lived, the witness at one point said that they had a good cooperation and that she remembered some people and she remembered the name of a man called Patrick. And then the Defence showed her a photograph where Mr. Patrick could be seen, and she said she recognised him. So I just informed the Prosecution about this, that perhaps within the questions about the cooperation with UNPROFOR and the assistance in -- bearing in mind her profession, what kind of cooperation they had. And on Saturday, I informed in a brief note my colleagues that she will also be speaking about the presence of UNPROFOR in the part of city where she lived and worked during the conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No more specifics about the witness Henneberry as far as I understand. Yes. Well, then the consequences of whatever shortcomings in the 65 ter might not be dramatic at this moment in respect of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, just another technical matter, I'm pleased that I have a new laptop at the Prosecution Bench this morning. I would be even more pleased if I were able to log on and make it work. I have tried and have some difficulties. So perhaps whilst --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm sure that the technicians provide you not only with the hardware, but also make it work. Anyone else that needs a new laptop?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Mine is still very ancient, as it always has been. And I just want to add two things: The Prosecution has just demonstrated brilliantly that like every day we have questions regarding detail. And linguistically, it is going rather well. But the second thing is the Defence is waiting more and more impatiently for the answers to the questions that the Defence asked in a language of the Tribunal regarding the cooperation between the parties and the uncontested points and we are awaiting this from the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber has noticed that sometimes the parties have expectations from each other which are not always fulfilled. But I take it that proper attention will be paid to it. Then, let's try and get the witness into the courtroom. Mr. Usher, could you please assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did hear you in a language which I do not understand, but I do understand the words "dobro jutro", so "dobro jutro" to you as well. And you can hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. The examination by Defence counsel will now continue. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday at the end of the day, we were cover a question that you didn't give the answer to. You said that on the 15th of April, 1992, after the duty that lasted for 25 days, you stopped going to work because in the institution where you worked some strange things were happening. Could you tell us very briefly what was so strange for you and that this strange things were a reason that you didn't go to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just one thing. I said it was mid-April. I'm not quite sure which day it was. I'm not quite sure which date this was. On that day, I noticed, just like my other colleagues, that within the closure of the hospital, there were some persons present that we didn't notice before. There was specifically -- particularly dressed, and it was unthinkable to see someone on a motorcycle driving around the hospital compound considering that there shouldn't be so much noise around the hospital. People were going with berets with some insignia, and some of these persons were also armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, after you stopped going to work, can you tell us that day in April 1992, did you continue to work in another place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After my last day at work, I was at home. I was waiting to get a call to come back to work because my work time was specific. I worked 25-hour shifts. But because my neighbours knew that I was a nurse, what happened was that there was an explosion near my house. And the -- and they said that my neighbour, Mirko Stupar, was wounded. And they asked me to come and administer first aid, to bandage his wound.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now that you've told us that you assisted your neighbour who was wounded, could you tell us when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the second half of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how was he injured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about weapons, but they told me that it was a grenade launcher, and that it was fired from the other side, from our neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that was a grenade launcher, that it was fired from the other side from your neighbours, are you telling us in that part of town where you lived, was there some kind of partition, division?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not until then. But one street was specific. On one side, Serbs lived on one side, and on the other side Muslims lived. It was just one ordinary street. And until that point, we always had good relations. I didn't know many people around there, but I knew some people.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us, what was the part of the town or the locality where you lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a part of the airport locality. This is local commune Roza Hadzivukovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if in 1992, after assisting your neighbour, were you engaged anywhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that event, I got a call to create some kind of an outpatient clinic, a kind of surgery. And myself and a neighbour, who is also a nurse.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Your engagement and the establishment of a clinic, together with your neighbour, you said that was upon a call. Who called you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was -- these were the people who organised themselves to defend our building. It was a kind of Crisis Staff, a kind of Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, you joined the Territorial Defence of your local commune?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you told us that you, together with your neighbour, you established a kind of team, you formed a kind of team, can you tell us if you had a location where you were, where you did this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a house, I think it was a Serbian house. Some people, and they had tenants on the lower floor. And these tenants left so what we did was we made a kind of first-aid room. We only had some bandages, just minimum requirements.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Can you tell us, in September 1992 --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: -- So that will be from 1992 through to 1994, where were you and where were you engaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1992, that is, from April, the second half of April, that is, until the end of April, I was near my house. That is in the -- at the airport locality. After that, a medical corps was created within Nedzarici, for the entire area. And I joined that group. There were several nurses there. We didn't have a doctor.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us, this medical corps as you called it and this large group of nurses, where were you? Where was your accommodation? Did you have any location inside Nedzarici where you were stationed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in the barracks. It used to be a medical clinic. It was like a surgery as part of the barracks, and that's where we established the medical corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, can you tell us whether throughout the time, from 1992 to 1994, as a nurse, were you in the medical corps in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while, we were in the barracks, but we had problems. Our security was at risk in this respect. And then we moved to the faculty of theology, that is, to the convent.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us, when did you go to the faculty of theology? When did you move there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date. I think it was in June -- no, no. It was in May, I'm sorry. It was in May.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you be precise; which year?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you moved to the faculty of theology in May 1992, can you tell us if this faculty of theology had been used by someone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, priests used it. Religious personnel used it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us until when were they there at the faculty of theology?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the end of April, I think, because just a little bit before we entered, they left.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you told us that you came as part of the medical corps, the medical department, to the faculty, at the end of May, you personally, how long did you stay at the faculty of theology?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there until 1993, mid-1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In that period, from May 1992 until mid-1993, while you were at the faculty of theology, can you tell us whether as part of that institution there were some other services apart from you in the medical department, those who were -- who else was in that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a group of mortars [Realtime transcript read in error "motors"], of mortar crews, people who were serving the motors, and an armoured unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, as a member of the medical corps, did you have a need to be engaged in that period in terms of assisting people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, when you say "of course," can you tell us, what was the reason that you felt the need to assist people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, there were many wounded and many people killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us, did you have any vehicles that you used? Was it necessary to engage vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had several vehicles because every vehicle that we had didn't last very long.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that you had several vehicles and that neither of them last very long, what did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the first vehicle that we had, it was an ambulance. It was an old vehicle, like a Lada vehicle but slightly longer. It was quite old. And it was riddled with bullets. After that, we had to improvise other vehicles that were not made for that purpose, so we had to make an addition in order to put in the stretcher.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that these vehicles were riddled with bullets, can you give us an example in which situation were these vehicles exposed to fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To start with, from April 1992, we did not, near the institution where we could take the severely wounded, we didn't have a place close by but we had to go across the runway, across the airport. We went [Realtime transcript read in error "won't"] to the Kasindol hospital, which was located --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. While you were at the faculty of theology, you told us that there was an armoured unit there. Can you tell us, and do you have any knowledge, whether as part of that armoured unit, there were vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what kind of vehicles they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Inaudible]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the answer because the interpreters could not hear you. Perhaps you'll come a bit closer to the microphone so that the interpreters can hear you better. Would you please repeat your answer on the question: "What kind of vehicles these were"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just one thing: To say this for the transcript, and I'm doing it now. In line 10, 9, of the current page, I'm not sure that at the end of line 9 it should not be -- it should not read as [In English] "we won't."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's "we went."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. And I just wanted to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the last part of that answer was either inaudible or -- you told us about the Kasindol hospital, and you were about to say where it was located. Where was that located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It was located near -- it is located near Lukavica. That is, you had to go across the runway. There was a corridor during the war, and it was on the other side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that within your building, an armoured unit was accommodated which had APCs, as you said. Can you tell us how many APCs there were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Those three APCs, were they used by you as members of the medical corps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be a problem hearing. Could you please repeat the question, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, the APCs, the vehicles that were within your premises, were they housed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, as members of the medical corps, have a need to use them, you personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 60 per cent of the cases, they had to assist us.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "in 60 per cent of the cases they had to assist you," can you tell us -- give us an example of the way in which they helped you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When shooting was intensive, we didn't dare go because our safety was at risk. In that case, we had to use the APC to go and fetch the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that you used the APC to get the wounded, can you tell us how frequently you and your colleagues extended aid to wounded persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many times a day. During one day, we would have to go two or three times to extend aid in 1992. Later on, it was less intense, less frequent.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you're telling us that in 1992, several times a day, and then in 1993, not quite so frequently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said not as frequently as in 1992. If I understood your question correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Let me clarify. In 1993, you said that you didn't go as frequently as in 1992. Can you tell us how frequent it was in 1993, if you said that in 1992 it was many times a day, several times a day? What was the incidence in 1993? Was it every day or once a week?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The witness said "two or three times a day" in 1992, not "several times".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do agree with you. On the other side, I don't think that that would create great confusion. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, Your Honour, that the witness said during the day, several times in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it says somewhere two or three times but then it says many times. But let's just proceed. I don't think that this would create -- that this would confuse the witness, and that's what it is about. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So please, will you answer my question regarding 1993. How frequent was it in 1993 that you extended aid to the wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you the numbers. I'm afraid you didn't understand me. It was -- there was shooting every day, and it was in that context that I answered your question, whether the crew of the APCs assisted us to fetch the wounded. There were cases when we could cross the meadow, extend first aid, and reach a spot where we were safe by car.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the transcript. Again, in the English transcript there is a gap. There is a gap, I must say what I heard in line 14, it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We usually do not -- it's uncontrollable, so if there's a gap, please point at it and ask the witness to repeat what the witness said at that moment because we cannot check what was said or what was not said. So please point to the gap and we'll ask the witness to repeat what she said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. But it is important for the follow-up of the cross-examination of Ms. Pilipovic. This gap on page 13, line 14, the witness indicated the frequency, and it was very clear from what she said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so we'll ask her to repeat what she said. You, according to the English transcript said: "I'm afraid you didn't understand me. It was, and then there was a certain part which does not appear in our transcript. And then you continued, there was shooting every day. Could you tell us again what you said. So after you said "I'm afraid you didn't understand me," it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that you didn't understand me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I understood the question of Mrs. Mara, it was whether the crew of the APCs assisted us. And I was answering the question with respect to the APC. Was that your question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Ms. Pilipovic, if you be informed by Mr. Piletta-Zanin what actually is missing, then you perhaps clarify the issue. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The words used by the witness that are missing which was "every day."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think it was quite clear that I do not allow you, if something does not appear in the transcript, to tell us what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's, of course, on the basis of the experience of the last few days. So would you move to your next subject, Ms. Pilipovic. I gave you in advance a warning not to tell us what the witness said. I did not allow it to you, so move to your next subject, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that you extended aid every day during 1992, during the day frequently, that there were a large number of wounded. Can you tell us whether the institution in which you worked was exposed to the activities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The witness did not use the word "every day." This is a follow-up from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, what happens as a matter of fact is I invited you to ask the witness to repeat what she said because it seems to be important. I did not allow Mr. Piletta-Zanin to tell us what the witness said. If it's really of that great importance you always could check us during the break on the original tapes if you want to do that. But Ms. Pilipovic, the only thing you now did is to repeat what -- in your answer when you said: "Perhaps you do not understand me," were you're telling that on a daily basis, you were assisted by those who had the APCs or did you say that on a daily basis, you would go out and assist the wounded people? What exactly did you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me explain. Sometimes, it would happen that there was a lot of shooting, so it was risky for us to go, so we used the APC. And sometimes we were able alone with an ambulance to reach a particular spot which wasn't so risky. Every place was risky, but still, there were places that we could access the wounded. Is that what you meant, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just have a look. Let me just seek to clarify the issue. You told us that sometimes you used the ambulance when there was not intensive shooting, so you dared to go without the assistance of the APCs. Could you tell us first for 1992, you told us that you would go out many times, two or three times a day. Would that be usually with the APCs or usually with the ambulance, or what would be the balance between the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With both means. I beg your pardon. May I explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- What I consider to be important. There was wounding every day. The position is such that we didn't know exactly where the front lines were. We knew where the greatest risk was, and when we were informed that we had a wounded person to attend to, if there is a lot of shooting, then we had to request the assistance of an APC if the person had been seriously wounded. Sometimes if the wounds were not so serious, we would wait for the shooting to subside, and then we would go to that position up to a point that we considered to be safe. Have you understood me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did understand you. And then now for 1993, because you told us that you went out not as frequent as in 1992. You told us for 1992 that it was many times, two, three times a day. What would be the frequency in 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sometimes there would be a pause for one day, but there was wounding in 1993 and in 1994 and in 1995. I was in Nedzarici until 1993. After that, I was in a hospital, and then I can tell you about that period when I was in hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand you well that you say it was on a daily basis, although not on every single day, that you went out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Logically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And how many times a day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Several times. You said it was in 1993, it was less frequent, not as frequent as in 1992. You told us that in 1992, it was -- you said many times, and you also said two or three times a day. Could you tell us how many times a day in 1993 on average?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't answer in that way. Whenever it was necessary. I cannot remember now how many times during the day. I can't tell you how many times every day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you said not as frequent as in 1992. That is correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1993, our men were organised in a slightly different manner because of the events that took place, they could distinguish what was urgent and what was not urgent, in which situations we could wait for the shooting to subside. Have I made myself clear?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think you did so. So my last question in this respect, in 1993, would you also use both an ambulance, if possible, and an APC, if necessary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We used the ambulance every day, and the APC only when it was risky for us to go in an ambulance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, before, we discussed this difference between 1992 and 1993, I asked you whether the building of the theology faculty was exposed to what I would call "activities" of weapons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "yes," can you tell us from which positions and how frequently the fire came? Do you know from which positions fire was opened at the building in which you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The witness never said the fire came. That is an interpretation by the Defence counsel. Witness only said that the building was exposed to activities. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then Ms. -- Yes, what activities did you have in mind apart from being exposed to fire coming from somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, my objection is based on the fact that it's leading. Perhaps the counsel should ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm afraid that the trial would then take another year. I think it's perfectly well asked. If there's a small leading element in it, it's not something that could create -- that would not influence the witness in such a way that it would be not acceptable. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you say that you didn't know from which positions fire was opened at the building in which you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you have any knowledge or do you remember that a certain point in time your building and you were photographed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally own those photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before I show the witness these photographs, I should like to ask the witness to tell us, if she can, when the building in which you were staying was photographed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: That is, what is the date of those photographs?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence, with your permission, would like to show the witness these photographs that the witness tells us are her own property, in her personal possession, and that they were photographs taken in front of the building of the theology faculty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I've no problem that you show the photographs, but that you tell the witness already what she will testify about the photographs is not -- you're going to tell us where they were taken, et cetera. If you would just show the photographs and then put questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before that, if I may be permitted to see the photographs because we have been given notice of photographs. I wonder whether they are the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I take it that these are the same photographs that you disclosed to the Prosecution, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Additionally, Mr. President, if I may point out that in the 65 ter summary, there's no mention whatsoever of the theology -- faculty of theology. In fact, the only mention is that of a hospital in Nedzarici, Zica hospital. So this is completely new material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any mention of the faculty of theology in any of the summaries, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in our summary, we said that the witness was employed in the hospital as of 1993. But we did notify the Prosecution, and the summary says that she was a member of the Territorial Defence in the area in which she lived. And that she worked as a nurse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's another word for an answer that is no, isn't it? Ms. Pilipovic, the faculty of theology has played a considerable role in the examination of many witnesses in this Court. It would have been appropriate to mention that this witness has stayed in the building for quite some time. That would have been appropriate in a summary. Let's just now first check whether the photographs are the same. I take it -- when did you receive these photographs?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Two days ago, Mr. President, when this witness was supposed to come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we have received them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. Perhaps we should -- would you please take it from the ELMO. And Ms. Pilipovic, if you asked for facial distortion, it's --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, could we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we can turn into closed session. And may we have a redaction for the, especially for the video. It did not go on the ELMO. Private session will do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session. We'll adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, and in order to avoid whatever confusion, where the English transcript, before the break, talks about motors and motor crews near to the faculty of theology, it should be mortars. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleague will continue with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I have your permission, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, if you know, a little about the cooperation between your service and the UN forces. What do you know about it? What could you tell us about that, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that in the initial period in 1992, that is, from the moment I was engaged, in the vicinity of the hospital, there was no institution for surgeries in April 1992. At the end of April 1992, the Zica hospital was formed but it didn't have a surgery theater. So that when we judged a patient to be serious, we had to cross the airport runway to go to the Kasindol hospital. At first, we crossed normally because at first, I don't know until when, the Serbs were at the airport. Later, foreigners arrived at the airport, and they had control over it. And we would inform them - I don't know who exactly - that we had a serious patient. We would go to the entrance to the runway. We would report to them. They would have to examine -- look at the patient and judge for themselves what kind of patient he was, and then they would give us permission to cross the runway. We were often accompanied by an APC until we left the runway, and then we would enter an area like a neutral area, a no man's land, I suppose. I do know that on -- the Serbs were on one side and the Muslims were on the other. And then we would drive the patient to the Kasindol hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Regarding the use of this neutral area, when you were entering with your vehicles, were there any incidents? And if yes, can you tell us anything about them briefly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I crossed the area, that is, the runway, I know the man -- the name of the man. I shall never forget that. His name was Klimenta Dusan. And as we were crossing, the Serb forces I think were still there. I'm not sure. This was in the month of May. And they opened fire at our vehicle. So that night, we didn't dare return. It was already dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'll stop you there. Thank you very much. Was your vehicle hit by the shots; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you able to establish, judging by the side from which those shots came and hit the vehicle, where they were coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was there a village or a district to the right of your vehicle at the time of the shots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Butmir district.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you know what type of weapon was used to fire at you, as medical personnel, while you were at the airport?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No evidence has been led that the vehicle was marked as a medical vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question reads: "Do you know what type of weapon was used to fire at you, as medical personnel?" Perhaps it might be unclear. Perhaps you could ask the witness first whether the car was recognisable as -- by any sign that it was transporting wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke to us a moment ago -- no, I'll withdraw that. The time that those shots were fired, was there any sign on your APC or whatever it was that could identify it as a medical vehicle; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were crossing using an ambulance. We were crossing the airport in an ambulance. And all our ambulances, whether they were improvised or not, always bore the Red Cross mark on them. Sometimes in the form of a flag --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For reasons of time, I'm interrupting you. You have answered the question, but I would still like you to be more precise. Later, after this attack, nobody was able to establish by the calibre of the holes, if any, what kind of weapon was used from Butmir. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Leading question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I hardly have ever seen --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Yes, but would you also refrain from doing it because it's of no use to first put a leading question to the witness and Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 15161 to 15170. then to rephrase it because the damage has been done then already. Yes, perhaps I would... An earlier question to you was, Ms. DP7, whether you knew what weapon was used when you were driving on the runway of the airport from the Butmir area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we just felt it whiz, the bullet whizzing past, but what kind of bullet it was I really don't know. It was sufficient for us to hide and to accelerate and move on, full speed. And because of this incident, we didn't dare return that same night across the runway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did it hit the car, or you said you heard it whiz while passing by the car. Was the car hit or was the car not hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The vehicle was hit. The glass broke into tiny pieces. And when we left, we could see the holes in the vehicle. But what kind of weapon, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please, then, move to your next subject, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Just another question to make things quite clear: Do you know at the time who held the Butmir village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you tell us who it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Still talking about -- no, we'll come to that later. Madam Witness, in the area of Nedzarici, did you know of an institution that was known as an old people's home, Dom Staraca in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know where it was situated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The old people's home was close to the school I attended for four years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the 65 ter summary, there is no reference to the old people's home either. So -- or the school. This is all new material which has not been -- we have not been given notice of this evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is my understanding correct that we discussed at least a couple of days ago, I think it was approximately one week ago, an article in direct relation to the old people's home and of which we --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to clarify this type of problem for the last time. I've already spoken of this, and the next time I will appeal to the presidency of the newly formed association of attorneys. In English, we would like to inform you, et cetera, that this witness will, yes, this witness will testify on the presence of UNPROFOR forces at Nedzarici. We know where they were before the 3rd of September, 1993. This was the subject of an animated debate in this courtroom. If we are now told that the text is not clear even though we mentioned this, this is false, once again. And the next time, I will appeal to the representative of the attorneys' association because this cannot continue in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, strong words do not necessarily make strong arguments. So to whom you're going to appeal, this Chamber will wait and see if it is -- if it does concern us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. May I -- your argument was not that it was said at a late stage; the argument was that you were not informed about it. That is as far as I can see in a letter of the 2nd of November, not true. So please, would you continue, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I have the opportunity to respond to that. Excuse me. Mr. President, we don't have that letter. I have a letter of the 3rd of November, which states that this witness will testify about the presence of UNPROFOR forces in Nedzarici and in collaboration with them -- excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I correct myself, Mr. President. We do have that letter. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I should like to intervene, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to intervene, Mr. President. This is not the first time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I am not -- it's perfectly clear that if an objection is based on a letter which has been sent to the Prosecution and if the objection is based on absence of knowledge of the content of that letter and if the next thing is that the Prosecution says that they did not receive that letter, and has to correct itself one minute later, then we lost a couple of minutes. I would say approximately the same number of minutes we lost yesterday when there was an objection which did find no basis in the transcript. It's up to me, then, to tell the Prosecution that this is a waste of time, just as it was a waste of time yesterday. The most important thing is that this will not happen, not by any party, and we'll now continue with the testimony of this witness. And there's no use in one party using, although it might be fairly justified under these circumstances, using strong words against the other. Please proceed. It's the Chamber who expressed the words just spoken. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, I should like to come back to the question that I raised. Where was this institution? You answered "next to your school." But in order to localise it, could you please give us the name of the street that we know that we're talking about the same thing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact name of the street but I do know where it is situated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Could you tell us whether it is situated to the south of Nedzarici, in the north of Nedzarici, or maybe close to this or that district that you're familiar with, facing such and such a district?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would come from our institution, that is, from the faculty of theology --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, let me interrupt you. Do you know whether this institution for the elderly was facing a particular district; and if so, which one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Close by was the institute for blind children.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. In relation to this institute for the elderly, and if you know, could you tell us which -- what was the ethnicity of the people there on the assumption that they were still there when you were staying in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were people, old people, of all ethnicities were housed there. There were old people, but there were a couple who were younger that I met during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Witness, do you know whether this institution was used for any other purposes than to provide accommodation for the elderly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know whether international institutions were able to visit this location? I'm specifically referring to UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know. We would see them frequently as the trucks, large trucks, would arrive. And I assume they were delivering food and medicines to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know whether these people from UNPROFOR used that building for other purposes than to provide humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that they checked what was happening in our district, that they were controlling what was happening in our district.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. When you told us that they controlled what was happening in your district, did you ever hear or see a delegation of the UN forces come to the convent or the theology faculty to protest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you tell us that you don't know, does that mean that you never heard of it or that you have no knowledge of it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The witness has answered "I don't know." And thereafter, it's not fair for the Defence counsel to ask the witness to elaborate on that question further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we usually allow, if the answer is "I don't know that" to see whether this is positive knowledge of nonoccurrence, or whether this is just ignorance on whether it happened. Let me just, if I would ask you, whether it was raining this morning and you say "I don't know," then it depends on whether you have been outdoors and have been able to observe whether it was raining or not, or that you just didn't notice -- well, there are different ways of saying I don't know. So we always accept it that the next question could be to have been confirmed whether it's positive knowledge of nonoccurrence or that it's just lack of knowledge whether it occurred or not. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My example was not a very good one, but I'll find out a better one if you need one. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I will put the same question slightly differently, and perhaps you can give me a yes or no answer. Did you ever hear that protests were formulated by these UN forces while you were staying at the theology faculty; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now place on the ELMO, in agreement with the Prosecution, Mr. President, the photographs from Exhibit P3274, and we can begin the one -- the last figures being 95, of which the last figures are 95. It relates to incident 22 on which both parties have already discussed, which both parties have discussed. Could we focus on the spot where the arrow is, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, to your right, there is a photograph. My first question is: Do you recognise this spot? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, do you recognise, more specifically, the buildings, the small houses appearing right beneath the arrow in the middle of the photograph? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, those houses, could you tell this Chamber at the time of the events, that is, at the time of the war, which party had control of them? In whose hands was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm very grateful. I will be grateful not to tell us anything at all that relates to your own personal experiences. Very well. Thank you. Witness, with the topographical knowledge that you have, I'd like to ask you the following question: Do you know or do you recognise the location from which this photograph may have been taken? The intersection in the foreground of the picture; yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This part, towards the arrow --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I apologise. If you can recognise it, just say yes or no. If you can, just say yes. If you can't, then say no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, now this is the question, and I'd like you to focus because I believe that you could answer with a yes or no. From the background of the photographs, so I'm saying the background of the photograph, behind the line or the lines of small houses that we see in the background, was it possible, according to your knowledge of this area, to fire horizontally with a rifle, for instance, and to hit the intersection that we see in the foreground of the photograph; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Why, why was this a direct hit not possible as we say, according to your knowledge of the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These houses belonged to Muslims. And much further behind were Serb houses that went as a kind of on a slope. They were lower than these houses here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam, close to the arrow that you have in the centre of the photograph, is there any facility, symbolic, cultural, anything like that at all, religious?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What do you know about this mosque during the war? I'm talking about possible -- probable destruction or no destruction in relation to the mosque. What do you know about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions -- no, just a moment. Yes, very last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell us if you know how many civilians, as far as you know, were in the area that you covered suffered -- were wounded, were physically hit by -- during the operations, war operations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilians, well, I don't know the exact number, but I know there were many.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you say "many," could you please -- no, I'll rephrase. When you say "many," could you give us any information about the location where these persons were wounded? Was this, for instance, near a confrontation line or more in the rear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the rear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Ms. Mahindaratne, is the Prosecution ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The photographs may be left with the witness for a moment. Mr. President, with the permission, may the witness be shown photograph C of the same series.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of the same sequence. Could the other photograph be returned -- or do you need that as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Madam, you have two photographs before you. Do you agree that photograph numbered C is a close-up of photograph numbered B?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, if you examine the two houses you can see in photograph C, would you agree that they are the very same houses which are below the arrow on photograph number B? Madam, I'm referring to those two little houses below the arrow in photograph number B. Are they the very same as those big houses in photograph number C, those two houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't understand where the arrow is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If you examine photograph numbered B, you will see an arrow, black arrow.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There are two houses, small houses, below that arrow. Could you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This part here? You mean this part here?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an arrow which shows, points --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the photograph, if the witness points at a certain part of the photograph, it should be put on the ELMO so that we can see where she points at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I'm not quite certain what you mean. Do you mean these houses here?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, these two houses below the arrow. If you just place your pointer on those two very small houses you see below the black arrow. Yes, I'm referring to those two houses.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These ones here. These are houses that belonged to Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. Now, if you examine photograph number C, which is a close-up of the same picture, you will see those two same houses bigger than in photograph number B. If you could perhaps --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: -- Place that photograph on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You agree they are the same houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know when those two houses were built?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In which period of time? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Were those two houses there during the period September 1992 to August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not go down there to look at these houses. I really don't know. I know there was a smaller house. Whether this was rebuilt, I really don't know. Whether it had had an extension put on, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Madam, were you there during this period? [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The photographs may be returned, Mr. President. No, if it can be kept there for a moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Madam, if you look from that position into the distance, would you agree that you would be looking down that street towards the direction of Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't agree with you. It's a view towards the houses at the airport settlement. They were part of the Nedzarici district, but they were separated by water. It is more towards the settlement across the water. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know. This street is not in relation to your identity as far as I'm aware of. But, Ms. Mahindaratne, perhaps we should clarify that there's no misunderstanding whatsoever as to whether the witness recognises the exact locations that appear on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Madam, could you identify this particular area? When you said you did identify this area, what is this street? You testified about this area in your examination-in-chief. What is this street? What is the name of this street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Roza Hadzivukovic Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, bearing in mind the previous answer of the witness, and I'm going to check it, [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will not pursue this line of questioning. I will move on to another subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Madam, earlier you said that your knowledge of English was very little, to use your own words. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: When you say "very little" would you be able to communicate in English with an English-speaking person, a person who speaks in English?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not well. Perhaps I would be able to understand a word or two and then perhaps if it is a very short question, I could answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I withdraw that question. I'm sorry, I don't intend to pursue this particular line of questions either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed to your next subject, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Ierace will take over from this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Madam, had you been to the institute of theology before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Had you been inside any of the buildings before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Faculty of theology had a library which was accessible to all the citizens, particularly those who went to that school, citizens of all ethnic background. And we were all able to have a membership card and to use the books from the library.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I take it you had a membership card and you used the library, is that correct, before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I went to the library, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, there were some 50.000 books in that library, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that the complex of the institute consisted of four buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can make a drawing of what the convent looked like, if you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, that would be good.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a complex --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the witness could be given a sheet of paper and a pen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, you certainly have a piece of paper. I take it that you'll invite her to draw something. If that could be done on the ELMO, that would be preferable. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, firstly, do you agree that there were four buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will clarify, and then you can establish whether it's true or not. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the entrance that you went in through the gate. This was the main entrance gate. It was like a corridor, like a hallway. From that part, this was a slightly higher building. You went into that building. And this part here went this way. And it was a lower building. This is where the exit was where we sat. Now, from this large part, there was a hallway, a corridor, which was a second part. The back part and the front part. So this part in the middle was empty. That was a garden. On the side where some other facilities -- ancillary facilities. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, that's good. Now, one of those buildings was essentially accommodation for the students. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean the lower building -- no, the taller building, the higher building was the one for students, and the lower building, as far as I know, because I was in one of the rooms, I think that used to belong to the lecturers of this faculty and during the war it burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. If you possibly could keep your answers as short as you can, I would appreciate it because we don't have much time. Have you shown on the diagram the tallest --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- Building that had the accommodation? Is that already on the diagram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The taller building faced the Vojnicko Polje. You understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Could you please point to it with the pointer on the diagram.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the taller building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Don't mark anything yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please carefully listen. If you're asked to point at something, do it with the pointer. And if you're asked to mark something or to draw something, do it then with the pen. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think you told us that you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was that a four-storey building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Three storeys.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you mean a ground floor with three storeys on top or do you mean a ground floor with two storeys on top?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ground floor, had a kind of mezzanine, and it was like a one floor. I think there were three floors -- three storeys. We didn't go all the way up, to that part we didn't go much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please listen to the question. Do you mean ground floor, and then above the ground floor, another three storeys? Or if you don't know because you didn't go up, then just tell us that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness is not aware of the difference, the whole system of the ground floors. There are two different ways of expressing yourself. If you say a three-storey building, some people mean to say that there's a ground floor and then three storeys up. Other people use that term for indicating that there was a building with one ground floor and then two storeys up. So if you say a three-storey building, was it a ground floor plus three or was it a ground floor plus two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Three storeys, the building had three floors. Believe me, I didn't count the storeys. I didn't go all the way up. I know it's a taller building compared to the one where we were. You understand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. That will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please place the letter A inside that building, the one we have just been discussing, on the diagram.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] It's this part here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now, was there another building which contained the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kitchen?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please place a K inside that building, after you have drawn it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't draw this very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's all right. Did that building have just a ground floor, or did it have more floors on top of the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was another floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, was there a building which had in it a church and theatre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said earlier, I think, that there was a building which had a room in it where the lectures were. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, all right. Was there a building which seemed to have, before the war, accommodated the teachers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Would you please place inside that building, if it already appears in the sketch, the letter B.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, I think there is another building between the A and the K on the sketch. What was inside that building? What was it used for before the war, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that part, this lower part, there was an amphitheatre.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: An amphitheatre. All right. Do you know if there was a chapel in that building before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. But I do know that -- may I? May I clarify something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In respect to this question. But there was a room on the side of the building, somewhere around here, the one that I'm drawing just now. And it was one room that we, in the beginning, used when we had a dead person. And this is where we would prepare him, wash him, and then he would be transported to the Vlakovo cemetery. So this may have been a chapel before the war; I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. In the building which had the amphitheatre, please place the letter C.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And whilst that's being done, may I ask the Madam Registrar to prepare to be shown to the witness photograph P3279T, and the ERN ending in the number and letter 3A.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now, there was a courtyard in the middle of those buildings. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: By the time you arrived in the faculty, I think you said that was around April of 1992, is that correct, that you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was the end of May, but I couldn't tell you the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Were the books there in the library?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to this question. I really don't see the relevance of this. First of all, there were 50.000 works, and now whether to find out whether the books are in order on the shelves. I really don't see the relevance of the Prosecution's question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question has been put and the question has been answered, but if you could inform us about the relevance, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps it could be done in the absence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if it's -- I'd rather -- will you continue in this line, because then we have to deal with it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll perhaps hear from you later and there's no use to ask the witness to leave the courtroom at this very moment. So please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The institute was a Catholic educational institution, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you don't know this, please tell me. It was of the Franciscan order of the Catholic church. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know what they were called. It was a faculty of theology. That's how we called it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Might the photograph be shown to the witness, if Madam Registrar has it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Usher, could you please assist.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P3279T, with the ERN ending 3A?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the photograph be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the photograph before you, do you recognise the institute as it appeared after the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the photograph, in the photograph, do you see the institute? That is, the faculty of theology, or the institute of theology?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness now points to the white building one-third down the middle of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which of the buildings is that, having regard to the sketch that you've given us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the highest building, the one with three storeys.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And on your sketch, I think you indicated that with the letter A. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, is the height of the building, as best you can tell, as it appears in the photograph, the height of the building as it was when you first arrived at the institute after the war commenced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're saying, what you really mean. Whether it was enlarged, expanded or not, was that your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll withdraw that question.
